action_horizon.action: Create a ranked watchlist and verify each thesis

contradiction_notes: The item calls one name a poor long while still identifying it as a short-term recovery buy.
units.evidence_sought: Rate sensitivity, debt refinancing needs, balance sheets, company-specific catalysts, and valuation.
units.falsifier: Rates fail to lower financing costs, or company-specific fundamentals negate the macro tailwind.
units.inference: Use macro easing as a screening lens, then distinguish firms with durable demand and manageable financing from those with structural risks.

raw_codes.label: Macro-to-company screening
raw_codes.rationale: Starts with monetary conditions but applies company-specific filters.

raw_codes.label: Refinancing sensitivity
raw_codes.rationale: Debt cost is a stated transmission channel.

units.trigger: A rate cut and broad sector selloff alter financing conditions and entry prices across growth assets.
uncertainty_notes: The many individual ratings have uneven evidence and several rely on assertion.

action_horizon.action: Differentiate and selectively buy insulated peers

units.evidence_sought: Customer concentration, contract counterparties, tenant funding, CDS or credit indicators, and each company's financing exposure.
units.falsifier: Hyperscaler-backed contracts weaken, or the supposedly insulated companies have material indirect tenant exposure.
units.inference: Buy sector participants insulated by hyperscaler contracts while avoiding names directly dependent on the troubled tenant.

raw_codes.label: Counterparty-risk mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Traces tenant credit risk through cloud providers and downstream suppliers.

raw_codes.label: Credit-contagion separation
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis fails if supposed insulation is not real.

units.trigger: A sector selloff follows concerns about a major tenant's creditworthiness and debt-funded capacity expansion.
uncertainty_notes: Claims about tenant obligations and contract backing need verification.

action_horizon.action: Research and monitor the 800G ramp

units.evidence_sought: Customer concentration, warrant economics, order conversion, production capacity, and hyperscaler demand.
units.falsifier: Orders do not convert, domestic manufacturing is not a procurement advantage, or major customers reduce demand.
units.inference: A supplier can offer asymmetric upside when a specific infrastructure ramp and geopolitical sourcing preference are not reflected in valuation.

raw_codes.label: Hyperscaler supply-chain mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Connects custom-chip deployments to a component supplier.

raw_codes.label: Domestic manufacturing advantage
raw_codes.rationale: Uses production location as the differentiating attribute.

units.trigger: A small photonics supplier has hyperscaler exposure, domestic manufacturing, and a large order signal while trading below thematic peers.
uncertainty_notes: The claimed customer relationships and implied warrant revenue require confirmation.

action_horizon.action: Accumulate for operational turnaround

units.evidence_sought: Cost savings realization, deal terms, revenue conversion, user trends, free-cash-flow impact, and buyback execution.
units.falsifier: Cost savings or monetization fail to materialize, or user decline damages revenue more than expected.
units.inference: A re-rating can occur from free-cash-flow improvement even if user growth remains weak.

raw_codes.label: Free-cash-flow re-rating
raw_codes.rationale: Focuses on converting revenue and cost cuts into cash generation.

raw_codes.label: Tax-harvest reversal
raw_codes.rationale: Uses the anticipated end of selling pressure as an entry catalyst.

units.trigger: A depressed consumer platform has identifiable cost cuts, possible new monetization, cash consideration, and buybacks.
uncertainty_notes: The free-cash-flow estimate is modeled rather than reported.

action_horizon.action: Buy selectively after validating backlog interpretation

units.evidence_sought: Whether backlog is contractual floor versus forecast, demand durability, product mix, and exposure of related suppliers.
units.falsifier: Backlog is not a durable contractual floor or subsequent orders fail to support expected revenue.
units.inference: A price reaction to an expectations miss can be a buying opportunity if minimum contracted demand preserves the core capex thesis.

raw_codes.label: Expectations-versus-floor dislocation
raw_codes.rationale: Distinguishes a minimum backlog disclosure from the market's implied forecast.

raw_codes.label: ASIC supply-chain read-through
raw_codes.rationale: Transfers the backlog interpretation to component suppliers.

units.trigger: A broad AI selloff follows a reported backlog figure below elevated expectations despite strong reported earnings.
uncertainty_notes: The asserted distinction between contractual floor and expected demand needs source verification.

action_horizon.action: Use a longer-duration expression of the thesis

units.evidence_sought: Underlying secular demand, valuation, options positioning, time horizon, and historical analog suitability.
units.falsifier: The structural demand thesis fails or the historical analog is not comparable.
units.inference: Separate directional thesis from instrument and timing: shares or longer duration may better express a crowded secular view than short-dated calls.

raw_codes.label: Time-horizon mismatch
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts short-dated option timing with longer-term thesis realization.

raw_codes.label: Retail-crowding interpretation
raw_codes.rationale: Treats crowding as potentially wrong on timing rather than direction.

units.trigger: Retail enthusiasm creates short-dated-options losses in a theme with a plausible long-term structural driver.
uncertainty_notes: The historical examples are anecdotal and may not generalize.

action_horizon.action: Build a post-selloff watchlist

units.evidence_sought: Company-specific causes, prior contract milestones, valuations, and liquidity after the selloff.
units.falsifier: Subsequent information shows the declines were driven by shared fundamental impairment.
units.inference: A broad drawdown is a screening event, not itself a buy signal; separate broken names from indiscriminate declines.

raw_codes.label: Indiscriminate-selloff screen
raw_codes.rationale: Uses wide price dispersion to identify candidates for fundamental triage.

raw_codes.label: Company-specific verification
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly avoids treating all declines alike.

units.trigger: A single-day sector-wide drawdown affects companies with different fundamentals.
uncertainty_notes: The item itself does not perform the company-by-company verification.

action_horizon.action: Re-underwrite the contracts at current prices

units.evidence_sought: Contract status, revenue conversion, balance-sheet changes, and reasons for the lower current price.
units.falsifier: The contracts are impaired, delayed materially, or offset by worse financing and execution risk.
units.inference: Compare current valuation with the information set at contract announcement to test whether the market has over-discounted later risks.

raw_codes.label: Below-contract-announcement price
raw_codes.rationale: Uses a historical information benchmark for re-underwriting.

units.trigger: Companies trade below prices prevailing before previously announced major contracts.
uncertainty_notes: Price alone does not show whether later risks are justified.

action_horizon.action: Monitor legislative passage and project-level permitting

units.evidence_sought: Legislative status, exact applicability, implementation dates, permitting schedules, and asset monetization impact.
units.falsifier: The legislation fails, excludes relevant projects, or does not reduce actual construction and interconnection delays.
units.inference: Faster permitting can pull revenue forward and reduce utilization drag for capacity builders, if the bill becomes operative.

raw_codes.label: Permitting acceleration
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed law is treated as the direct catalyst.

raw_codes.label: Permits-to-cash-flow chain
raw_codes.rationale: Links review timing to deployment, utilization, and revenue recognition.

units.trigger: A proposed permitting reform could shorten data-center construction and litigation timelines.
uncertainty_notes: The practical effect depends on bill text, enactment, and implementation.

action_horizon.action: Reassess affected infrastructure and component suppliers

units.evidence_sought: Funding terms, tenant use of proceeds, enforceability of chip adoption, supplier exposure, and counterparty concentration.
units.falsifier: Funding does not support contractual obligations or the hardware-adoption condition is not implemented.
units.inference: Tenant funding can reduce counterparty risk downstream while redirecting demand into a specified hardware supply chain.

raw_codes.label: Funding-to-supply-chain ripple
raw_codes.rationale: Traces investor funding through tenant capacity spending to component demand.

raw_codes.label: Counterparty recapitalization
raw_codes.rationale: New funding is the proposed de-risking event.

units.trigger: A major investor funds a capacity-constrained AI tenant and requires adoption of its proprietary chips.
uncertainty_notes: The deal terms and downstream demand allocation are not verified in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Assess contracted-capacity economics
action_horizon.horizon: Over the 15-year lease and deployment milestones

units.evidence_sought: Contract duration, minimum versus optional capacity, backstop terms, buildout obligations, and expected cash flow.
units.falsifier: The counterparty does not draw capacity, the backstop is weak, or project delivery fails.
units.inference: A long-duration, backstopped lease can materially improve revenue visibility and re-rate a small infrastructure provider.

raw_codes.label: Credit-backed contract
raw_codes.rationale: The named backstop is central to contract quality.

raw_codes.label: Contracted-capacity valuation
raw_codes.rationale: Lease economics support a reassessment of value.

units.trigger: A capacity lease with a creditworthy backstop is announced for an infrastructure provider.
uncertainty_notes: The optional capacity and project costs are not described.

action_horizon.action: Reassess counterparty-risk discounts

units.evidence_sought: Funding completion, cash proceeds, contractual obligations, exposure by provider, and concurrent macro positioning effects.
units.falsifier: The fundraising fails to close or proceeds are insufficient relative to obligations.
units.inference: Improved tenant financing can relieve a sector-wide counterparty-risk discount, especially for directly exposed providers.

raw_codes.label: Tenant balance-sheet improvement
raw_codes.rationale: The funding event is the stated reason for reduced risk.

raw_codes.label: Sector-leader sentiment transmission
raw_codes.rationale: Links tenant funding to providers and then correlated assets.

units.trigger: A higher-valuation funding round improves a major tenant's perceived financial capacity and lifts related assets.
uncertainty_notes: Other cited drivers, including volatility and memory demand, confound the price reaction.

action_horizon.action: Underwrite adoption and reserve-income scenarios

units.evidence_sought: Reserve composition, interest-rate sensitivity, transaction and adoption data, regulation, competitive shares, and charter status.
units.falsifier: Network adoption stalls, regulation weakens the model, or declining rates overwhelm growth in reserves and usage.
units.inference: Evaluate the issuer as payments infrastructure with network effects and reserve economics rather than solely as a crypto proxy.

raw_codes.label: Infrastructure versus fintech framing
raw_codes.rationale: Reclassifies the business model for valuation purposes.

raw_codes.label: Reserve-income and network effects
raw_codes.rationale: Identifies the proposed economic engines.

units.trigger: A stablecoin issuer is framed as benefiting from reserve income, settlement-network adoption, and regulatory alignment.
uncertainty_notes: Claims of implicit state support and inevitable settlement dominance are speculative.

action_horizon.action: Model supplier revenue by platform and customer

units.evidence_sought: Bill-of-material content, customer spend, supplier share, margins, competitive alternatives, and design-win duration.
units.falsifier: Content share is lower than modeled, spending does not materialize, or competitors displace the supplier.
units.inference: Translate customer capex into supplier revenue using architecture-specific content share rather than broad thematic exposure alone.

raw_codes.label: BOM share-of-spend model
raw_codes.rationale: Estimates supplier economics from platform bill-of-material content.

raw_codes.label: Competitive displacement
raw_codes.rationale: Identifies future competing suppliers as the principal downside.

units.trigger: A supplier is embedded in multiple accelerator architectures and has unusually high content in one customer's design.
uncertainty_notes: The BOM percentages and future customer spend are informal estimates.

action_horizon.action: Track platform-specific ramp milestones

units.evidence_sought: Platform deployment schedules, supplier design wins, production capacity, and relative valuation.
units.falsifier: The identified platforms do not ramp or the supplier lacks the claimed design role.
units.inference: Identify underfollowed suppliers of less-publicized platform ramps rather than extrapolating from the best-known winner.

raw_codes.label: Platform-specific supplier mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Assigns suppliers to particular hyperscaler architectures.

raw_codes.label: Attention-gap valuation
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts media attention between supply chains.

units.trigger: Different component suppliers are levered to distinct hyperscaler chip ramps while attention favors one platform.
uncertainty_notes: The claimed platform relationships and ramp outcomes are uncertain.

action_horizon.action: Monitor qualification and production milestones

units.evidence_sought: Unit volumes, BOM allocation, customer qualification, manufacturing capacity, schedule, and alternate suppliers.
units.falsifier: The supplier fails reliability qualification or loses the design win to an alternative supplier.
units.inference: A small supplier's upside can be transformative when a large platform ramp converts, but qualification failure should be the gating risk.

raw_codes.label: Platform BOM scenario model
raw_codes.rationale: Uses unit and BOM assumptions to estimate supplier-scale impact.

raw_codes.label: Qualification failure
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly identifies technical qualification as the decisive risk.

units.trigger: A projected ASIC ramp implies a large supplier opportunity, but supplier qualification is uncertain.
uncertainty_notes: The author labels the modeling speculative and notes no public BOM breakdown.

action_horizon.action: Monitor capacity allocation and material supply indicators

units.evidence_sought: Supplier market shares, substrate capacity, customer inventory, alternative technologies, and demand growth.
units.falsifier: Market concentration is overstated, capacity expands sufficiently, or architectures materially reduce input dependence.
units.inference: A concentrated upstream input can become the binding constraint and pricing power locus in a downstream infrastructure boom.

raw_codes.label: Upstream bottleneck
raw_codes.rationale: Material scarcity is the proposed transmission mechanism.

raw_codes.label: Input-to-AI deployment dependency
raw_codes.rationale: Links substrate supply to optical systems and accelerator clusters.

units.trigger: A concentrated upstream material market is required for expanding optical interconnect deployment.
uncertainty_notes: Market-share estimates are approximate and internally qualified.

action_horizon.action: Track supply constraints and customer allocation behavior

contradiction_notes: The item alternates between a duopoly and a wider group supplying the market.
units.evidence_sought: Material availability, supplier capacity, optical-component lead times, customer pre-allocation, and substitute architectures.
units.falsifier: Supply expands, demand forecasts are overstated, or silicon-photonics and copper alternatives remove the dependency.
units.inference: Map a hardware bottleneck to upstream substrates; scarcity could produce price increases, stockpiling, and deployment delays.

raw_codes.label: Bottleneck cascade
raw_codes.rationale: Traces demand from clusters to optics to substrates.

raw_codes.label: Technology substitution
raw_codes.rationale: Alternative architectures are the stated escape route.

units.trigger: Optical interconnect demand may exceed high-purity substrate supply across several accelerator programs.
uncertainty_notes: Demand and shortage magnitudes are sourced as estimates and may be inconsistent.

action_horizon.action: Monitor feedstock supply and geopolitical restrictions

units.evidence_sought: Feedstock purity requirements, producer shares, trade flows, captive supply, export controls, and alternative sourcing.
units.falsifier: Feedstock is readily substitutable, producer shares are inaccurate, or nonconcentrated supply can meet laser-grade requirements.
units.inference: Extend supply-chain analysis one level upstream because feedstock concentration can constrain nominally diversified substrate supply.

raw_codes.label: Bottleneck within bottleneck
raw_codes.rationale: Moves analysis from substrates to their critical feedstock.

raw_codes.label: Geographic supply concentration
raw_codes.rationale: Country concentration is treated as a strategic risk.

units.trigger: A concentrated substrate bottleneck may itself depend on concentrated high-purity upstream feedstock.
uncertainty_notes: Producer-share estimates and feedstock dependence are asserted without primary documentation in the item.

action_horizon.action: Treat as a tail-risk bottleneck scenario and monitor shortages

units.evidence_sought: Material share of BOM, inventory levels, price elasticity, capacity constraints, historical shortage analogs, and geopolitical exposure.
units.falsifier: The material is not binding, buyers can substitute it, or capacity meets demand without price escalation.
units.inference: When delay costs greatly exceed input costs, buyers may bid aggressively for scarce inputs, creating nonlinear pricing and supplier upside.

raw_codes.label: Critical-material bidding dynamic
raw_codes.rationale: High delay cost relative to material cost drives potential price escalation.

raw_codes.label: Nonlinear scarcity optionality
raw_codes.rationale: Frames the supplier as an upside scenario rather than linear TAM growth.

units.trigger: A low-cost critical material may become a bottleneck for very high-value hardware deployments.
uncertainty_notes: The extreme price scenarios are analogical and explicitly speculative.

action_horizon.action: Wait for earnings evidence before increasing conviction
action_horizon.horizon: Next earnings cycle to two-to-three years

units.evidence_sought: ARR conversion, EBIT margins, capex, dilution, cash balances, institutional ownership, and upcoming earnings.
units.falsifier: Margins fail to scale, cash burn and dilution persist, or backlog does not convert to cash flow.
units.inference: The key re-rating gate shifts from growth and funding to demonstrated unit economics and execution.

raw_codes.label: Prove-it phase
raw_codes.rationale: Reframes prior growth-driven valuation around the next needed proof point.

raw_codes.label: Dilution-to-cash-flow transition
raw_codes.rationale: Identifies repeated capital raising as a central concern.

units.trigger: High-revenue-growth infrastructure firms have financing but markets await evidence of scalable margins and cash flow.
uncertainty_notes: Projected ARR, margins, and price targets remain forward estimates.

action_horizon.action: Buy only after verifying order coverage and program timeline

units.evidence_sought: Current purchase orders, design freeze status, chip-development timelines, customer qualification requirements, and scope of alternative suppliers.
units.falsifier: Purchase orders are cancelled, the design is not frozen, or the competitor takes the relevant production scope.
units.inference: Distinguish future-generation diversification from immediate replacement; physical design and validation cycles can make mid-cycle displacement unlikely.

raw_codes.label: Displacement-timeline test
raw_codes.rationale: Tests bearish reports against engineering and procurement timing.

raw_codes.label: Rumor-driven selloff
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed opportunity originates in a perceived misinterpretation of reports.

units.trigger: A selloff follows reports of potential supplier displacement mid-development on a complex custom-chip program.
uncertainty_notes: Engineering timelines and rebuttals to media reports are not independently verified in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Screen beaten-down names for a January recovery trade

units.evidence_sought: Three-month and year-to-date decline, earnings outlook, tax-loss selling evidence, balance-sheet risks, and January performance.
units.falsifier: The decline reflects a broken fundamental thesis or seasonal selling does not reverse.
units.inference: A seasonal mean-reversion trade is appropriate only after excluding names with genuine fundamental impairment.

raw_codes.label: January-effect mean reversion
raw_codes.rationale: Uses year-end selling pressure as a seasonal entry condition.

raw_codes.label: Fundamental quality filter
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly conditions the trade on nonbroken fundamentals.

units.trigger: Fundamentally viable stocks suffer sharp year-end losses potentially driven by tax-loss selling.
uncertainty_notes: Seasonal effects are probabilistic and may not recur.

action_horizon.action: Build thematic research maps and update them as constraints change

units.evidence_sought: Technology constraints, value-chain participants, adoption readiness, commercial beneficiaries, and second- or third-order effects.
units.falsifier: The proposed constraints are not binding or named beneficiaries lack meaningful exposure.
units.inference: Classifying themes by mechanism helps locate investable beneficiaries beyond the most visible end-product companies.

raw_codes.label: Evolution-disruption-bottleneck taxonomy
raw_codes.rationale: Provides a reusable framework for organizing thematic research.

raw_codes.label: Second- and third-order mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly seeks downstream and upstream beneficiaries.

units.trigger: Technology themes are organized by whether they evolve existing systems, disrupt incumbents, or relieve bottlenecks.
uncertainty_notes: The broad newsletter contains numerous unverified thematic assertions.

action_horizon.action: Maintain distinct recovery and long-term thesis buckets

units.evidence_sought: Whether each decline is seasonal versus fundamental, company-specific drivers, valuation, and horizon consistency.
units.falsifier: A supposedly seasonal decline is structural, or thematic assumptions fail.
units.inference: Separate short-term mean-reversion trades from long-term thematic holdings instead of applying one rating framework to both.

raw_codes.label: Horizon-separated ratings
raw_codes.rationale: The item explicitly distinguishes short-term trading from long-term views.

raw_codes.label: Post-tax-harvest recovery
raw_codes.rationale: Year-end selling is used as a recurring entry thesis.

units.trigger: A new-year ratings list combines tax-harvest recovery candidates with longer-term thematic beneficiaries.
uncertainty_notes: The large rating list provides uneven depth and mixes diverse risk profiles.

action_horizon.action: Monitor export permits, price spreads, and capacity allocation

units.evidence_sought: Lead times, component bookings, spot and export prices, supplier cost structure, permits, and substrate pricing.
units.falsifier: Exports are restricted, price spreads close, or upstream demand does not materialize.
units.inference: An upstream integrated supplier may capture both scarcity pricing and geographic cost arbitrage when downstream capacity is locked.

raw_codes.label: Upstream scarcity migration
raw_codes.rationale: Moves from booked finished goods to substrate and feedstock demand.

raw_codes.label: Cross-market margin arbitrage
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis depends on low-cost production and higher export pricing.

units.trigger: Capacity reservations in finished optical components may push hyperscaler demand upstream to substrates and feedstock.
uncertainty_notes: Price, supply-share, and demand-propagation claims require independent verification.

action_horizon.action: Map direct operational beneficiaries after confirming events

units.evidence_sought: Actual disruption scope, commodity substitution, refinery configuration, procurement needs, and company exposure.
units.falsifier: The disruption does not occur, supply is readily replaced, or companies lack meaningful operational exposure.
units.inference: Avoid generic sector proxies; identify assets tied to the disrupted grade, logistics route, or operational capability.

raw_codes.label: Event-to-specialized-beneficiary mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Maps disruption through commodity quality, logistics, and military operations.

raw_codes.label: Avoid generic proxies
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts specific exposure with broad oil or defense exposure.

units.trigger: A geopolitical disruption threatens specialized export flows and creates military operational demand.
uncertainty_notes: The underlying event and many company-specific claims are unverified in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Monitor political recognition, sanctions changes, and contract awards

units.evidence_sought: Political transition durability, sanctions, debt recovery terms, advisor mandates, infrastructure contracts, and operational assets.
units.falsifier: Political transition reverses, sanctions persist, debt recovery is poor, or reconstruction contracts do not materialize.
units.inference: Map post-regime-change opportunities across debt recovery and reconstruction bottlenecks rather than limiting analysis to oil producers.

raw_codes.label: Regime-change reconstruction chain
raw_codes.rationale: Traces the event into debt, advisory, infrastructure, logistics, and refining.

raw_codes.label: Distressed-asset recovery
raw_codes.rationale: Uses discounted debt recovery as a specific valuation mechanism.

units.trigger: A regime-change scenario could reprice distressed sovereign debt and require reconstruction, financial advisory, logistics, and refinery capacity.
uncertainty_notes: Scenario outcomes, debt recoveries, and contract allocations are highly uncertain.

action_horizon.action: Build a scenario-weighted creditor watchlist.

units.evidence_sought: Award enforceability, claim seniority, auction proceeds, recovery timing, and market capitalization.
units.falsifier: Claims are subordinated, unenforceable, or recovery proceeds are insufficient.
units.inference: Compare realizable claim recoveries or asset swaps with enterprise value; separate cash-recovery cases from higher-risk asset-return cases.

raw_codes.label: Legal recovery catalyst
raw_codes.rationale: A court auction or settlement can convert claims into cash or assets.

raw_codes.label: Claim-to-market-value comparison
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis compares recoverable value with current capitalization.

units.trigger: Regime change coincides with large creditor claims trading below potential recoveries.
uncertainty_notes: Recovery amount and timing are explicitly uncertain.

action_horizon.action: Track the basket against stated weights and catalysts.

units.evidence_sought: Each holding's direct exposure, valuation, liquidity, and allocation-level downside.
units.falsifier: The event does not produce the assumed access, funding, or demand for the listed companies.
units.inference: Express one macro event through a diversified basket spanning claims, commodities, logistics, and defense rather than a single name.

raw_codes.label: Thematic basket construction
raw_codes.rationale: The post translates one macro view into weighted exposures.

raw_codes.label: Geopolitical reconstruction
raw_codes.rationale: Expected policy and reconstruction drive the basket.

units.trigger: A geopolitical regime-change thesis creates several purported beneficiary routes.
uncertainty_notes: Company-specific links to the event are asserted rather than demonstrated.

action_horizon.action: Monitor seizure and disposition announcements before positioning on supply effects.
action_horizon.horizon: Near term through multi-year custody period

units.evidence_sought: Custody evidence, ownership, seizure status, legal constraints, and liquidation policy.
units.falsifier: The reserve does not exist, is inaccessible, or is promptly liquidated.
units.inference: Model custody outcomes separately: locked assets reduce float, while forced sale raises supply; price direction depends on which outcome occurs.

raw_codes.label: Custody-to-float transmission
raw_codes.rationale: Legal custody changes available supply, which may affect price.

raw_codes.label: Forced-sale scenario
raw_codes.rationale: A rapid sale reverses the proposed lock-up effect.

units.trigger: A potentially seized, concentrated asset stockpile could change tradable supply.
uncertainty_notes: Reserve size and custody outcome are highly speculative.

action_horizon.action: Wait for program details and map direct versus indirect beneficiaries.

units.evidence_sought: Official subsidy terms, eligible recipients, allocation size, required private capex, and refinery/service compatibility.
units.falsifier: No subsidy is enacted, or funding is too small or broadly distributed to change economics.
units.inference: If public funding replaces private capex, beneficiaries may rerate through lower funding needs and higher project economics.

raw_codes.label: Subsidy reduces capital burden
raw_codes.rationale: Government funding is the proposed source of changed project economics.

raw_codes.label: Policy-to-rerating chain
raw_codes.rationale: Funding is expected to affect capex expectations and valuation.

units.trigger: Prospective public subsidies alter the capital burden of a sector expansion.
uncertainty_notes: The post labels allocations beyond the lead company as speculative.

action_horizon.action: Monitor subsequent revenue recognition and backlog conversion.

units.evidence_sought: Backlog quality, shipment timing, booking-to-revenue conversion, management execution record, and peer-multiple comparability.
units.falsifier: The shortfall reflects cancelled demand or recurring execution failures rather than deferral.
units.inference: A delayed shipment can create a valuation dislocation only if backlog converts and the lower multiple is not caused by execution risk.

raw_codes.label: Deferred-revenue dislocation
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed entry follows a price fall attributed to delayed shipments.

raw_codes.label: Forward-sales multiple gap
raw_codes.rationale: Valuation is assessed against estimated sales and peers.

units.trigger: A small defense company trades at a lower sales multiple after a shipment-related revenue miss.
uncertainty_notes: The author acknowledges execution uncertainty and limited diligence.

action_horizon.action: Verify competitor constraints and customer qualification before treating the supplier as a monopoly.

units.evidence_sought: Control scope, affected competitor capacity, substitute suppliers, and the focal firm's usable capacity.
units.falsifier: Competitors retain supply access or customers can qualify alternatives.
units.inference: A supply restriction can improve a remaining supplier's pricing power only if it can serve displaced demand.

raw_codes.label: Export-control supply shock
raw_codes.rationale: The claimed catalyst is a restriction on a competitor.

raw_codes.label: Substitution risk
raw_codes.rationale: Alternative supply would defeat monopoly economics.

units.trigger: An export-control change may remove a competitor from a concentrated supply market.
uncertainty_notes: The post does not substantiate the claimed monopoly.

action_horizon.action: Map the supply chain and test whether input availability constrains output.

units.evidence_sought: Material intensity, supplier market share, inventory, qualification cycles, and alternative technologies.
units.falsifier: Memory or another component, not the input material, is the actual constraint.
units.inference: Trace a widely recognized demand bottleneck backward to constrained inputs, but require evidence that the small supplier is binding.

raw_codes.label: Upstream bottleneck mapping
raw_codes.rationale: The argument links AI demand through materials to a supplier.

raw_codes.label: Supply-chain lens
raw_codes.rationale: It examines dependencies rather than headline demand alone.

units.trigger: A downstream AI bottleneck is alleged to depend on a small upstream materials supplier.
uncertainty_notes: The assertion that one small supplier bottlenecks the entire buildout is unverified.

action_horizon.action: Validate technical product boundaries and customer facts before adding.

units.evidence_sought: Product architecture, affected component scope, customer confirmation, and revenue exposure by use case.
units.falsifier: The new architecture displaces the company's products or signals lost customer demand.
units.inference: Buy a selloff only when the alleged adverse development does not affect the company's actual product layer.

raw_codes.label: Headline-misinterpretation dip
raw_codes.rationale: The entry is predicated on an allegedly immaterial selloff.

raw_codes.label: Product-scope verification
raw_codes.rationale: The move distinguishes internal and external connectivity exposure.

units.trigger: A sharp stock decline follows headlines that may misdescribe product exposure.
uncertainty_notes: The longer-term transition to photonics is acknowledged as a risk.

action_horizon.action: Track contract conversion and continuing-segment margin disclosures.

units.evidence_sought: Contract records, actual deployment confirmation, segment margins, backlog, cash, and divestiture financials.
units.falsifier: The claimed deployment is not tied to the company, or margins and demand do not persist after the sale.
units.inference: Use operational deployment as product validation, then reassess valuation on the continuing high-margin segment rather than blended legacy economics.

raw_codes.label: Operational-validation evidence
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis seeks links from named operations to company equipment.

raw_codes.label: Continuing-segment repricing
raw_codes.rationale: The argument relies on a more profitable remaining business.

units.trigger: A defense contractor's equipment is linked to current military use while its post-divestiture margins improve.
uncertainty_notes: Several operational links are inferential rather than confirmed.

action_horizon.action: Monitor supply allocations and pricing after the restriction.

units.evidence_sought: Supplier shares, control applicability, constrained capacity, and customer sourcing behavior.
units.falsifier: The restriction does not impair competing supply or customers substitute away.
units.inference: A concentration thesis needs evidence that restrictions both constrain rivals and shift purchasable demand to the focal supplier.

raw_codes.label: Concentrating export control
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed monopoly follows a trade restriction.

units.trigger: Export controls may concentrate a critical input market among remaining suppliers.

units.inference: Exposure across several bottlenecks may provide diversified leverage to a broad buildout, subject to proving material participation.

raw_codes.label: Multi-node bottleneck exposure
raw_codes.rationale: Links substrates to memory, packaging, ASICs, and consumer devices.

raw_codes.label: Foundational component supplier
raw_codes.rationale: Frames value capture through indispensable substrate supply.

units.trigger: A supplier serves multiple constrained semiconductor nodes and major end customers.
uncertainty_notes: The breadth and criticality of customer relationships are asserted, not demonstrated.

action_horizon.action: Hold or reassess based on thesis evidence, not short-dated option losses.

units.evidence_sought: Whether policy, earnings, competitive position, and balance sheet changed rather than only the share price.
units.falsifier: The policy or national-security premise, operating fundamentals, or financial capacity deteriorate.
units.inference: Price volatility alone does not invalidate a longer-duration thesis.

raw_codes.label: Thesis-duration discipline
raw_codes.rationale: Separates near-term price movement from a longer expected catalyst timeline.

raw_codes.label: Fundamental-change test
raw_codes.rationale: Makes thesis change rather than drawdown the reassessment condition.

units.trigger: A stock falls sharply despite an asserted unchanged long-term fundamental thesis.
uncertainty_notes: The underlying policy thesis is not independently evidenced.

action_horizon.action: Verify program-level revenue exposure before treating it as a pure-play.

units.evidence_sought: Revenue attributable to the technology, program participation, competitors, and whether the company is a pure-play.
units.falsifier: The company has immaterial program exposure or a more direct competitor captures the economics.
units.inference: A company with direct relevant product exposure may provide more targeted thematic exposure than diversified peers.

raw_codes.label: Pure-play exposure screen
raw_codes.rationale: Frames the company as targeted exposure to directed-energy weapons.

raw_codes.label: Program association
raw_codes.rationale: Bases relevance on claimed use in named defense programs.

units.trigger: An investor seeks exposure to a narrow defense technology theme.
uncertainty_notes: Claims about orbital applications and program usage are not supported with evidence in the chunk.

action_horizon.action: Avoid treating strategic importance as sufficient; model fully diluted equity value and refinancing risk.

contradiction_notes: The text describes the company as a strategic bottleneck while calling the equity a financial landmine.
units.evidence_sought: Enterprise value, debt maturities, conversion terms, registered shares, cash burn, and scaling economics.
units.falsifier: Operating scale generates enough value to service debt and absorb dilution, or financing terms improve materially.
units.inference: Technology leadership can coexist with an equity-capital-structure trap; dilution and debt must be assessed separately from the product thesis.

raw_codes.label: Technology-versus-capital-structure split
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts monopoly-like technology claims with debt, converts, and registered shares.

raw_codes.label: Strategic asset, distressed equity
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly presents a bull-bear paradox.

units.trigger: A strategically valuable technology leader has substantial debt, convertibles, and registered creditor shares.
uncertainty_notes: The exclusivity and future interposer need are asserted.

action_horizon.action: Track qualification and adoption milestones before assigning revenue impact.

units.evidence_sought: Technology roadmaps, customer qualification, production readiness, material suppliers, and timing of adoption.
units.falsifier: The incumbent material remains in use or the proposed material does not reach commercial qualification.
units.inference: A proposed materials shift creates a research map across wafers, equipment, inspection, packaging, and downstream integrators.

raw_codes.label: Technology-stack mapping
raw_codes.rationale: Maps a possible SiC interposer transition through multiple supply-chain layers.

raw_codes.label: Early-research qualification
raw_codes.rationale: Explicitly characterizes the supply chain as early and research-active.

units.trigger: A potential future materials transition could alter a semiconductor packaging stack.
uncertainty_notes: The adoption timeline is speculative.

action_horizon.action: Update margin and earnings scenarios after confirming the reported price change.

units.evidence_sought: Confirmed contract pricing, estimate revisions, cost pass-through, product mix, and incremental gross-margin sensitivity.
units.falsifier: The report is inaccurate, pricing is not realized, or higher costs/volumes offset incremental margins.
units.inference: An upside pricing surprise can have disproportionate profit impact when incremental revenue carries high margins.

raw_codes.label: Pricing-surprise earnings leverage
raw_codes.rationale: Compares a reported 100% price increase with lower prior estimates and infers margin upside.

raw_codes.label: Incremental-margin sensitivity
raw_codes.rationale: Focuses on the conversion of pricing upside into gross margin.

units.trigger: A reported commodity price increase is materially above prevailing expectations.
uncertainty_notes: The price report and the asserted margin sensitivity require confirmation.

action_horizon.action: Map each material to a verified beneficiary rather than relying on thematic association.

units.evidence_sought: Material-specific supply concentration, restriction details, substitutability, domestic capacity, and beneficiary revenue exposure.
units.falsifier: Restrictions do not constrain supply, alternatives are readily available, or listed companies lack material exposure.
units.inference: Policy-driven supply-security efforts may create a screening universe of Western substitutes for restricted materials.

raw_codes.label: Export-control supply shock
raw_codes.rationale: Uses foreign export controls and government funding as demand/security catalysts.

raw_codes.label: Critical-material beneficiary map
raw_codes.rationale: Connects specific materials to proposed Western beneficiaries.

units.trigger: Export controls or government funding highlight critical-material dependencies.
uncertainty_notes: The stated beneficiary mappings are not evidenced in the chunk.

action_horizon.action: Track enacted policy and realized pricing/margins rather than political statements alone.

units.evidence_sought: Actual tariff treatment, subsidy terms, geographic capacity, competitor exposure, pricing, and margins.
units.falsifier: Policies are not implemented or do not improve the domestic producer's competitive economics.
units.inference: Policy can create an asymmetric domestic-production advantage, but its economic incidence must be verified.

raw_codes.label: Domestic-policy moat
raw_codes.rationale: Frames tariffs, grants, and domestic expansion as competitive support.

raw_codes.label: Policy-source claims
raw_codes.rationale: Relies on attributed government statements and reported policy developments.

units.trigger: Domestic producer economics may be affected by tariffs, subsidies, and capacity expansion.
uncertainty_notes: Tariff and subsidy effects on relative economics are inferred.

action_horizon.action: Compare expected yield with downside and growth scenarios before using dividends as a safety proxy.

units.evidence_sought: Total-return downside, business growth, valuation, dividend coverage, and drawdown history.
units.falsifier: The dividend strategy offers superior risk-adjusted total return under verified assumptions.
units.inference: Yield alone does not define safety; drawdown risk and business trajectory must be evaluated together.

raw_codes.label: Total-return versus yield lens
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts dividend yield with one-day drawdown magnitude.

raw_codes.label: Safety-definition challenge
raw_codes.rationale: Challenges a yield-based characterization of safety.

units.trigger: An investor equates a small dividend yield with safety despite potential large drawdowns.
uncertainty_notes: The claim that obvious growth companies are safer is unsupported and overgeneralized.

action_horizon.action: Research suppliers only after confirming the thermal-material transition path.

units.evidence_sought: Power roadmaps, thermal specifications, material qualification, supplier capacity, and design wins.
units.falsifier: Power designs solve thermal needs with incumbent materials or the anticipated transition is not adopted.
units.inference: Escalating power density can create a future niche-material bottleneck before market revenues appear.

raw_codes.label: Power-density material transition
raw_codes.rationale: Links higher power architectures to potential composite demand.

raw_codes.label: Pre-adoption research window
raw_codes.rationale: Places possible relevance before a projected 2027 transition.

units.trigger: Future chip power targets may require a material change in thermal management.
uncertainty_notes: The material need and supplier concentration are speculative.

action_horizon.action: Validate the proposed case-to-sink application and manufacturing route before assigning beneficiaries.

units.evidence_sought: Package-level thermal architecture, qualification data, manufacturing scalability, alternative materials, and customer adoption.
units.falsifier: Copper or other incumbents meet requirements, or AlSiC is not selected for the claimed package applications.
units.inference: A technical bottleneck thesis should identify the exact package interface where a new material captures value, while retaining alternative explanations.

raw_codes.label: Power roadmap to package-material demand
raw_codes.rationale: Traces higher TDP through heat flux, warpage, package interfaces, and material choice.

raw_codes.label: Interface-specific material capture
raw_codes.rationale: Locates possible value at the case-to-sink heat-spreader or lid interface.

raw_codes.label: Research-stage thesis
raw_codes.rationale: Calls the thesis ongoing research and frames the beneficiary as possible.

units.trigger: Projected accelerator power density may exceed the practical limits of incumbent thermal materials.
uncertainty_notes: Most technical adoption claims are prospective and unverified within the packet.

action_horizon.action: Compare balance-sheet risk and value capture across the customer-supplier pair.

units.evidence_sought: Debt burden, interest expense, contract economics, supplier revenue capture, collateral terms, and customer solvency.
units.falsifier: The supplier does not capture the financed spend or the customer generates sustainable returns that outweigh leverage risk.
units.inference: When financing recirculates into supplier purchases, the supplier may have cleaner exposure than the leveraged customer.

raw_codes.label: Bet on the supplier economics
raw_codes.rationale: Prefers the supplier collecting spending over the leveraged buyer.

raw_codes.label: Customer leverage screen
raw_codes.rationale: Uses debt and annual interest burden to distinguish exposure quality.

units.trigger: A capital-intensive customer receives financing or support from its key supplier.
uncertainty_notes: The casino analogy simplifies contractual and financing relationships.

action_horizon.action: Monitor supply withdrawal and legacy-product pricing for evidence of scarcity premiums.

units.evidence_sought: Capacity reallocations, legacy demand persistence, competitor exits, inventory positions, price data, and smaller producer capacity.
units.falsifier: Legacy demand falls faster than supply, competitors retain capacity, or new supply enters.
units.inference: A residual supplier can gain pricing power when legacy demand remains while incumbent supply is withdrawn.

raw_codes.label: Legacy-supply vacuum
raw_codes.rationale: Attributes upside to large producers leaving lower-end DRAM supply.

raw_codes.label: Residual supplier pricing power
raw_codes.rationale: Frames the remaining producer as capturing scarcity premiums.

units.trigger: Large producers shift capacity from legacy products toward higher-value advanced products.
uncertainty_notes: Capacity shifts and demand persistence require independent confirmation.

action_horizon.action: Value the existing business separately from the unproven AI option.

units.evidence_sought: Existing end-market revenue, balance-sheet resilience, AI qualification, material share, and adoption timing.
units.falsifier: Existing defense/space demand is not durable or the AI thermal use case does not materialize.
units.inference: Established non-AI demand may provide downside support while a new AI use case supplies optionality.

raw_codes.label: Base business plus optionality
raw_codes.rationale: Separates established defense/space usage from prospective AI thermal demand.

raw_codes.label: Niche-material chokepoint
raw_codes.rationale: Focuses on a claimed large share of AlSiC supply.

units.trigger: A niche material supplier has existing defense and space demand plus a possible new AI application.
uncertainty_notes: The AI application and market share are unverified claims.

action_horizon.action: Verify exclusivity and contracted demand before treating a small initial price move as mispricing.

units.evidence_sought: Exclusive production capability, government procurement, planned investment, capacity, and competing sources.
units.falsifier: Alternative domestic supply emerges, policy does not lead to orders, or capacity cannot expand.
units.inference: A strategically scarce domestic capability can be rerated when policy support translates into binding demand or investment.

raw_codes.label: Strategic domestic monopoly
raw_codes.rationale: Bases the thesis on claimed sole U.S. enrichment capability.

raw_codes.label: Nuclear-policy demand
raw_codes.rationale: Links energy policy and projected investment to demand.

units.trigger: A domestic producer is described as the only current provider of a strategic nuclear input amid policy support.
uncertainty_notes: The exclusive capability and investment statement need verification.

action_horizon.action: Use capacity plans as an upper-bound scenario and wait for production orders.

units.evidence_sought: Capacity announcement, actual production ramp, supplier content range, margin, and supplier ability to fulfill volume.
units.falsifier: The production line is delayed or underutilized, supplier content changes, or the supplier is not selected.
units.inference: Multiplying credible planned units by supplier content produces a scenario-based revenue sensitivity estimate.

raw_codes.label: Capacity-times-content sensitivity
raw_codes.rationale: Calculates potential revenue from one million units times dollars per unit.

raw_codes.label: Management-quote input
raw_codes.rationale: Uses attributed customer and supplier management statements as model inputs.

units.trigger: A customer announces dedicated production capacity for a new product and a supplier states per-unit content.
uncertainty_notes: The model assumes production capacity becomes realized demand and the content estimate remains applicable.

action_horizon.action: Withhold action until competing claims are reconciled using primary evidence.

contradiction_notes: The Reuters article and the company/agency statements present conflicting accounts.
units.evidence_sought: Original reporting, company release, agency statement, contracts, and objective operational evidence.
units.falsifier: The negative report is corroborated or contractual relationships are actually impaired.
units.inference: A disputed report can create a temporary informational gap, but neither denial alone establishes a buying opportunity.

raw_codes.label: Conflicting-source reconciliation
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts a media report with company and agency denials.

raw_codes.label: Disputed-headline review
raw_codes.rationale: Treats the drawdown as a prompt for verification, not automatic entry.

units.trigger: A sharp price decline follows a negative media report that is publicly disputed by the company and a government source.
uncertainty_notes: Both the report and counterclaims require independent verification.

action_horizon.action: Underwrite existing business value first, then assign probability-weighted value to AI adoption.

units.evidence_sought: Existing revenue and contracts, share of available supply, product qualification, cash/debt, manufacturing expansion, and AI customer design wins.
units.falsifier: Defense demand weakens, financial condition deteriorates, market share is overstated, or AI packaging does not adopt the material.
units.inference: A defensible base business can limit downside while a new high-growth application offers asymmetric optionality, provided the application is technically adopted.

raw_codes.label: Base-value plus technology option
raw_codes.rationale: Separates defense/government demand from prospective AI upside.

raw_codes.label: Sole-source niche materials
raw_codes.rationale: Uses claimed market share and single-customer designs as value-capture evidence.

raw_codes.label: Conditional material pivot
raw_codes.rationale: States AI upside depends entirely on adoption by large technology buyers.

units.trigger: A small materials company has current defense customers, claimed market share, and a speculative future AI application.
uncertainty_notes: AI adoption, market share, customers, and contract interpretation require independent verification.

action_horizon.action: Track revenue, free cash flow, and returns on incremental investment across earnings reports.

units.evidence_sought: Guidance, capex return profile, free cash flow, unit economics, and whether spend converts into revenue.
units.falsifier: Capex rises without corresponding revenue, cash flow, or return improvement.
units.inference: High capex is not necessarily bearish when operating evidence shows productive conversion into growth and cash generation.

raw_codes.label: Capex-as-investment versus expense
raw_codes.rationale: Tests whether capital expenditure is productive rather than value-destructive.

raw_codes.label: Guidance revision
raw_codes.rationale: Uses above-expected revenue guidance as a potential sentiment catalyst.

units.trigger: A large-cap company guides revenue growth above expectations while investors focus on elevated capital expenditure.
uncertainty_notes: The conclusion about future ROI is an inference from limited stated metrics.

action_horizon.action: Map counterparties and suppliers before inferring which downstream companies benefit.

units.evidence_sought: Contract terms, facility ownership, beneficiary revenue exposure, capacity allocation, and counterparties' product mix.
units.falsifier: The payment does not increase demand, is already reflected in contracts, or does not flow to proposed beneficiaries.
units.inference: Supply commitments can identify second-order beneficiaries in a shared manufacturing ecosystem.

raw_codes.label: Manufacturing-commitment spillover
raw_codes.rationale: Connects a supply-payment announcement to potential downstream beneficiaries.

raw_codes.label: Quoted contract disclosure
raw_codes.rationale: Anchors the observation in an attributed payment statement.

units.trigger: A major manufacturer commits a large payment for manufacturing services and continued supply.
uncertainty_notes: No specific second-order beneficiary is identified or quantified.

action_horizon.action: Update forward estimates and test whether the variance is recurring.

units.evidence_sought: Reported guidance, consensus estimates, reasons for the variance, sustainability, and valuation response.
units.falsifier: Guidance is not achieved or the variance is a one-off accounting, timing, or pricing effect.
units.inference: A large guide-versus-consensus gap is an earnings-revision catalyst, not merely a retrospective price argument.

raw_codes.label: Guide-versus-consensus surprise
raw_codes.rationale: Uses stated sales and EPS guidance versus estimates.

raw_codes.label: Earnings guidance
raw_codes.rationale: The key observation is reported forward financial guidance.

units.trigger: An earnings guide materially exceeds consensus for both revenue and EPS.
uncertainty_notes: The stated figures need verification and do not establish durability.

action_horizon.action: Differentiate inventory-arbitrage exposure from manufacturing-capacity exposure.

units.evidence_sought: Capacity shifts, legacy product demand, remaining producer capacity, inventory cost basis, and realized price changes.
units.falsifier: Legacy demand declines, major producers keep supplying the segment, or inventory cannot be monetized at higher prices.
units.inference: Inventory holders and remaining legacy-product producers may benefit from a supply vacuum created by higher-value product prioritization.

raw_codes.label: Legacy-storage supply vacuum
raw_codes.rationale: Links enterprise/AI pivots to reduced legacy NAND availability.

raw_codes.label: Inventory arbitrage versus capacity
raw_codes.rationale: Distinguishes lower-cost inventory from fab-based production as separate benefit paths.

units.trigger: Large producers redirect capacity from legacy storage toward AI-oriented products.
uncertainty_notes: The claimed production shifts and stockpile size require independent confirmation.

action_horizon.action: Monitor whether spot scarcity converts into supplier contract pricing and margins.

units.evidence_sought: Spot and contract prices, volumes, inventory, supplier capacity, customer demand, and upstream producer realization.
units.falsifier: Prices reverse, supply expands, or upstream suppliers cannot capture the price increase.
units.inference: Confirmed upstream price tightness can precede revenue and pricing power for qualified suppliers.

raw_codes.label: Upstream spot-price signal
raw_codes.rationale: Uses an all-time-high specialty-material price as the observable input.

raw_codes.label: Supply-shock transmission
raw_codes.rationale: Infers a path from precursor scarcity to supplier price increases.

units.trigger: An upstream specialty-material price reaches a new high during a claimed supply-constrained buildout.
uncertainty_notes: The asserted hyperscaler demand and inevitability of a supply shock are not verified.

action_horizon.action: Separate forced-liquidation mechanics from fundamental thesis before interpreting the drawdown.

units.evidence_sought: Exchange notices, margin schedules, open interest, leveraged positioning, fund premiums, halts, and cash-flow evidence of forced selling.
units.falsifier: Evidence shows a fundamental demand/supply shock rather than forced liquidation, or the cited market-structure events did not occur.
units.inference: Market-structure and leverage events can cause price dislocations independent of a change in long-term commodity fundamentals.

raw_codes.label: Margin changes to forced liquidation
raw_codes.rationale: Traces collateral changes through margin calls to selling pressure.

raw_codes.label: Market-structure versus fundamentals
raw_codes.rationale: Distinguishes paper-market mechanics from fundamental value.

units.trigger: A commodity price crash coincides with repeated margin-rule changes, elevated leverage, and cross-market trading disruptions.
uncertainty_notes: The claimed causal contribution of each event requires data verification.

action_horizon.action: Compare causal claims against primary exchange data before acting on the headline narrative.

contradiction_notes: The chunk explicitly conflicts with the media's stated causal account.
units.evidence_sought: Time-stamped exchange actions, market prices, positioning data, and primary reporting supporting competing causal narratives.
units.falsifier: Timing and market data support the reported macro explanation over the exchange-mechanics explanation.
units.inference: Competing crash narratives should be adjudicated by event timing and market-structure evidence, not rhetoric.

raw_codes.label: Competing crash-causation narratives
raw_codes.rationale: Contrasts media attribution with an exchange-rules explanation.

raw_codes.label: Primary exchange-evidence check
raw_codes.rationale: Requires moving from broad media claims to exchange records.

units.trigger: Media attributes a crash to a headline explanation while exchange-rule changes and market dislocations are alleged.
uncertainty_notes: The assertions about institutional motives and media suppression are unsupported.

action_horizon.action: Verify issuer identity and peer balance-sheet exposures before considering a sympathy-trade.

units.evidence_sought: Institution identity, size, receivership records, peer exposures, uninsured deposits, CRE exposure, and price correlations.
units.falsifier: The similar-name company has direct exposure, or broader peers show comparable balance-sheet risks.
units.inference: Name confusion or broad headline contagion can create temporary mispricing, but only if the failed institution is demonstrably isolated.

raw_codes.label: Entity-disambiguation screen
raw_codes.rationale: Separates similarly named financial institutions.

raw_codes.label: Headline-contagion mispricing
raw_codes.rationale: Identifies possible algorithmic or sector selling after a failure.

units.trigger: A small bank failure may generate sympathy selling in similarly named securities or a broader regional-bank sector.
uncertainty_notes: The explanation for the bank failure is speculative.

action_horizon.action: Map exposures by transmission channel rather than trade the headline label.
action_horizon.horizon: Near term through the policy transition

units.evidence_sought: Recent statements, balance-sheet preferences, sector transmission channels, and asset-specific exposure.
units.falsifier: Recent policy statements or implementation signals do not support rate cuts, balance-sheet reduction, or the proposed sector channels.
units.inference: Separate near-term rate policy from liquidity policy; the same official can support cuts while reducing balance-sheet liquidity, producing divergent sector effects.

raw_codes.label: Disaggregate policy channels
raw_codes.rationale: It distinguishes rate cuts, balance-sheet policy, regulation, and currency effects.

raw_codes.label: Policy to sector exposure
raw_codes.rationale: It traces policy stance through liquidity and regulation into sectors.

units.trigger: A policy appointment is being interpreted through an outdated single-label view.
uncertainty_notes: Policy intentions and sector effects are asserted rather than independently evidenced in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Validate normalized forward earnings across the memory group before treating the cycle as structural.

units.evidence_sought: Comparable forward net-income estimates, estimate dates, and consistency of company versus TTM measures.
units.falsifier: Updated estimates show the projected profits are not comparable, are reduced materially, or do not persist.
units.inference: A projected earnings surge can identify a cyclical profit inflection, but mixed forward and trailing comparisons need normalization.

raw_codes.label: Forward-profit comparison
raw_codes.rationale: The claim is based on projected net income across companies.

raw_codes.label: Normalize mixed periods
raw_codes.rationale: The post mixes 2027 forecasts with TTM figures.

units.trigger: Forward profit estimates imply a sector may become unusually large relative to current market expectations.
uncertainty_notes: The estimates are second-hand and use mixed measurement periods.

action_horizon.action: Reduce leverage and favor profitable, cash-generative exposures while monitoring whether liquidity stabilizes.

units.evidence_sought: Margin-rule changes, liquidation data, cross-asset correlations, funding conditions, and company cash-flow quality.
units.falsifier: Broad selling persists after liquidation pressure abates and earnings or policy evidence deteriorates.
units.inference: A forced-liquidation shock can create temporary contagion; distinguish liquidity-driven selling from a deterioration in underlying fundamentals.

raw_codes.label: Forced-liquidation contagion
raw_codes.rationale: The move is attributed to margin-driven liquidations spreading across assets.

raw_codes.label: Liquidity-versus-fundamentals reset
raw_codes.rationale: It frames selloffs as potential entry points only after separating causes.

units.trigger: A sharp move in one market coincides with broad risk-asset weakness.
uncertainty_notes: The causal chain and expected recovery are asserted without market data in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Refresh earnings models and compare normalized forward multiples before ranking memory exposures.

units.evidence_sought: Current analyst estimates, estimate freshness, DRAM/NAND price changes, and duration of the memory cycle.
units.falsifier: Updated estimates eliminate the valuation gap or memory pricing reverses.
units.inference: Compare cycle beneficiaries using updated forward P/E, but stale estimates can understate earnings when pricing changes rapidly.

raw_codes.label: Forward-multiple rerating
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed opportunity is low forward P/E amid rising earnings.

raw_codes.label: Estimate freshness check
raw_codes.rationale: The post flags that some analyst inputs are older than recent price data.

units.trigger: Peer forward multiples differ sharply despite a common demand cycle.
uncertainty_notes: Price increases and recalculated multiples are not independently verified.

action_horizon.action: Use extreme sentiment to begin diligence or staged entries rather than commit fully.

units.evidence_sought: All historical extreme readings, forward-return distribution, drawdowns, and regime comparability.
units.falsifier: A broader comparable sample shows extreme fear has poor or highly variable forward returns.
units.inference: Extreme fear can be a contrarian entry screen, not a standalone buy signal; three historical observations are insufficient for certainty.

raw_codes.label: Sentiment-extreme backtest
raw_codes.rationale: It compares returns after prior extreme-fear readings.

raw_codes.label: Contrarian staged entry
raw_codes.rationale: Fear is used to time a possible entry.

units.trigger: A sentiment index reaches an extreme level with few recent precedents.
uncertainty_notes: The sample is very small and does not establish causality.

action_horizon.action: Monitor whether earnings revisions continue before maintaining a cycle thesis.

units.evidence_sought: Forward earnings revisions, pricing durability, capacity additions, and peer valuation.
units.falsifier: Demand or price hikes reverse, causing forward earnings to fall and the multiple to expand.
units.inference: Price appreciation may not exhaust upside when earnings expectations rise faster than the share price.

raw_codes.label: Earnings-led valuation compression
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis rests on a low forward P/E after a rally.

units.trigger: A stock rises materially while its forward P/E remains low.
uncertainty_notes: The claimed structural nature of demand and price hikes is unverified.

action_horizon.action: Treat as a high-risk scenario position only after validating production and supplier economics.

units.evidence_sought: Production plans, revenue per robot, margins, customer commitments, and supplier share.
units.falsifier: Factory conversion, volume targets, or the supplier's economics do not materialize.
units.inference: Unit-volume scenarios can size upside, but revenue opportunity alone does not establish value capture or execution probability.

raw_codes.label: Volume-times-content scenario
raw_codes.rationale: The post estimates revenue from robot volumes and revenue per unit.

raw_codes.label: Moonshot sizing
raw_codes.rationale: It explicitly characterizes the idea as a moonshot.

units.trigger: A moonshot thesis extrapolates unit economics from a future production ramp.
uncertainty_notes: The production and revenue assumptions are estimates without support in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Recalculate owner economics including SBC and financing costs before taking a long position.
action_horizon.horizon: Next earnings and annual reporting cycle

units.evidence_sought: SBC, dilution, net debt, interest expense, buyback purpose, and cash FCF after compensation.
units.falsifier: SBC declines materially, repurchases are funded by excess cash, or underlying cash generation covers dilution and interest.
units.inference: Reported FCF can overstate shareholder economics when SBC dilution is offset by debt-funded repurchases.

raw_codes.label: Debt-funded dilution offset
raw_codes.rationale: The analysis links buybacks, debt, SBC, and interest costs.

raw_codes.label: Owner-earnings adjustment
raw_codes.rationale: The thesis depends on adjusting FCF for compensation and financing.

units.trigger: Reported adjusted profitability and prospective FCF coexist with unusually large stock-based compensation and debt-funded buybacks.
uncertainty_notes: Forward monetization and FCF components are estimates.

action_horizon.action: Build a conservative SOTP with explicit discount haircuts before pursuing an arbitrage.

units.evidence_sought: Net cash, value and liquidity of investments, operating FCF, liabilities, geopolitical discount, and governance risks.
units.falsifier: Asset values are not realizable, liabilities consume the apparent surplus, or operating performance weakens.
units.inference: A sum-of-the-parts discount may be investable only after separating realizable assets from the operating business and country-risk discount.

raw_codes.label: Sum-of-the-parts valuation
raw_codes.rationale: The post compares market value with cash and portfolio assets.

raw_codes.label: Realizability and geopolitical discount
raw_codes.rationale: These determine whether the apparent discount is genuine.

units.trigger: Market capitalization approaches cash or portfolio-asset value despite operating growth.
uncertainty_notes: Asset values and risk premia are not quantified in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Keep the position while memory prices rise; choose instruments based on volatility pricing.

units.evidence_sought: Memory-price trend, forward estimates, option IV versus realized volatility, and each instrument's exposure.
units.falsifier: NAND or DRAM pricing begins to fall or volatility makes the chosen option structure unattractive.
units.inference: Use instrument selection to express the same thesis: shares where call IV is expensive, cash-secured puts for entry premium, and options where upside path is steadier.

raw_codes.label: Price-trend exit condition
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed core holding lasts until memory prices show deterioration.

raw_codes.label: Instrument-fit expression
raw_codes.rationale: Different equities receive shares, puts, or calls based on IV and expected path.

units.trigger: A cyclical sector has low forward multiples and elevated option implied volatility.
uncertainty_notes: The claims about relative IV and expected price paths are unsupported in the packet.

action_horizon.action: Compare direct and fund exposures after validating the forward estimates.

units.evidence_sought: Forward earnings estimates, currency-adjusted access vehicle valuation, and cycle durability.
units.falsifier: Forward earnings estimates fall or regional vehicles trade at an offsetting premium.
units.inference: Rising prices do not necessarily imply expensiveness when forward earnings increase more rapidly.

raw_codes.label: Earnings outrun price appreciation

units.falsifier: Realized volatility stays low, new leveraged products do not gain scale, or IV already incorporates the risks.
units.inference: If structural volatility rises and is not incorporated into IV, long calls can gain through vega expansion as well as direction.

raw_codes.label: structural volatility expansion

raw_codes.label: vega exposure
raw_codes.rationale: The proposed value capture is option repricing rather than only price direction.

units.trigger: Long-dated index options price IV below expected realized volatility in a concentrated, newly leveraged market.

units.inference: A large IV gap may signal that long-dated options underprice a structural volatility regime.

raw_codes.label: long-dated IV discount

units.falsifier: Returns cannot be attributed beyond market beta, leverage, or chance.
units.inference: A trading process should distinguish repeatable catalyst categories from broad performance claims and manage concentration accordingly.

raw_codes.label: return attribution
raw_codes.rationale: Lists trades and outcomes for retrospective decomposition.

raw_codes.label: concentration management
raw_codes.rationale: States that outcome depends on more green exposure than red exposure.

action_horizon.action: Use long-dated options only after confirming the rotation and option sensitivity.

units.inference: A sector rotation can lift long-dated option value before options reach the strike.

raw_codes.label: institutional sector rotation

units.falsifier: A recession, higher rates, delayed power demand, or failure to secure grid funding breaks the combined thesis.
units.inference: Multiple independent tailwinds can support a utility/grid re-rating and make low-IV long-dated options a convex expression.

raw_codes.label: macro and capex convergence
raw_codes.rationale: Combines rates, investment, demand, and utility earnings effects.

raw_codes.label: historically low option IV
raw_codes.rationale: Uses low IV as the proposed implementation advantage.

action_horizon.action: Investigate assets that capture value from generation and grid expansion.

units.falsifier: Power constraints ease without incremental grid investment or do not translate into provider earnings.
units.inference: Repeated primary-source constraint signals can identify a bottleneck upstream of AI deployment.

raw_codes.label: AI deployment to grid demand
raw_codes.rationale: Maps a compute constraint to power and infrastructure demand.

uncertainty_notes: Executive statements establish concern but not the magnitude of earnings capture.

action_horizon.action: Attribute gains before updating conviction or repeating the trade.

units.evidence_sought: Pre- and post-thesis IV, option prices, realized volatility, and alternative return drivers.
units.falsifier: Option gains are explained by underlying-price movement or time effects instead of vega.
units.inference: The outcome supports the mechanism only if gains are attributable to IV expansion rather than directional movement.

raw_codes.label: mechanism attribution after outcome
raw_codes.rationale: The claim is a retrospective assessment of an IV call.

units.trigger: An option-IV expansion thesis has a favorable initial outcome.
uncertainty_notes: No decomposition of option returns is supplied.

action_horizon.action: Map the chain to identify the smallest supplier with direct bottleneck exposure.

units.evidence_sought: Supply shares, spot prices, competitor constraints, bill of materials, policy actions, and end-demand forecasts.
units.falsifier: The company lacks the asserted chokehold, supply expands, or end-demand fails to convert.
units.inference: Convergent evidence across the chain can reveal a bottleneck before earnings revisions capture it.

raw_codes.label: cross-source supply-chain synthesis
raw_codes.rationale: Synthesizes disparate evidence into a bottleneck thesis.

raw_codes.label: upstream choke-point exposure
raw_codes.rationale: Targets the supplier said to control substrate and feedstock.

units.trigger: Several independent supply-chain, pricing, policy, and capex signals point to one upstream bottleneck.
uncertainty_notes: The supply-chain relationships and market shares are not verified in the post.

action_horizon.action: Prioritize structural earnings support; use DCA or wait for correction in extended groups.

units.evidence_sought: Earnings revisions, capex timing, valuations, price extension, and hyperscaler guidance.
units.falsifier: Cycle timing is wrong or earnings evidence does not validate the claimed differentiation.
units.inference: Sector selection and entry timing should reflect cycle stage rather than treating all AI beneficiaries alike.

raw_codes.label: cycle-stage entry discipline
raw_codes.rationale: Differentiates memory, photonics, grid, and packaging by timing.

raw_codes.label: active monitoring requirement
raw_codes.rationale: Conditions the approach on earnings and capex monitoring.

units.trigger: Different AI-related bottleneck groups are at different points in their investment and earnings cycles.
uncertainty_notes: The described cycle timing is a subjective forecast.

action_horizon.action: Calculate look-through concentration before judging index diversification or option IV.

raw_codes.label: look-through concentration analysis
raw_codes.rationale: Counts indirect ownership and operating dependence, not only direct ETF weights.

raw_codes.label: rebalancing toward volatile constituents
raw_codes.rationale: Quarterly rebalancing is presented as a reinforcement mechanism.

uncertainty_notes: The look-through weights and IV forecast require independent calculation.

action_horizon.action: Research generation and grid beneficiaries with credible capacity expansion paths.

units.evidence_sought: Primary statements, utility interconnection queues, power-contract prices, and grid investment data.
units.falsifier: Capacity shortages resolve quickly or returns accrue elsewhere in the value chain.
units.inference: Power capacity is an upstream AI bottleneck that can support demand for utilities and grid infrastructure.

raw_codes.label: executive constraint testimony
raw_codes.rationale: Relies on statements by direct industry participants.

raw_codes.label: capacity bottleneck
raw_codes.rationale: Identifies constrained power supply as the catalyst.

units.trigger: Multiple major AI executives describe electricity and grid capacity as current constraints.
uncertainty_notes: Statements do not quantify duration, margins, or investable value capture.

action_horizon.action: Avoid concentrated short-dated option bets; define maximum premium loss first.

units.evidence_sought: Break-even move, time to expiry, probability distribution, premium-at-risk, and portfolio impact.
units.falsifier: The position is a deliberately limited-risk speculation within a diversified portfolio.
units.inference: A weekly option requiring a large immediate move has a high probability of expiring worthless and should not receive full-risk sizing.

raw_codes.label: short-dated option risk control
raw_codes.rationale: Provides a general sizing and instrument-risk lesson.

raw_codes.label: expiry break-even test
raw_codes.rationale: Uses the required move by expiry as a downside check.

units.trigger: An investor considers committing most capital to short-dated out-of-the-money options.

action_horizon.action: Use look-through exposure to estimate a sustainable volatility range.
